page.start.progress.label: Setup progress
page.start.welcome.title: Welcome to your first mesh
page.start.welcome.body: You'll create an account, a mesh, and a gateway that sends readings here. It takes about 10 minutes. Have the Meshtastic app open and a radio with Wi-Fi or Ethernet.
page.start.welcome.stepAccount: Create or sign in to your account
page.start.welcome.stepBasics: See how a mesh, a gateway, and a reading fit together
page.start.welcome.stepMesh: Name the mesh and its channel
page.start.welcome.stepGateway: Register the gateway and wait until a packet arrives
page.start.account.title: Create your account or sign in
page.start.checkEmail.title: Check your email
page.start.checkEmail.body: We sent a confirmation link to {email}. Open it and this step continues on its own.
page.start.checkEmail.notYet: That email is not confirmed yet. Open the link, then try again.
page.start.basics.title: How readings arrive
page.start.basics.lead: Nodes reach a gateway. The gateway publishes to MQTT, and Mesh Things stores the readings.
page.start.basics.mesh.title: Mesh
page.start.basics.mesh.body: A mesh is one radio network: a channel name and a key. Mesh Things decrypts what arrives on that channel.
page.start.basics.gateway.title: Gateway
page.start.basics.gateway.body: A gateway is the radio that forwards the mesh over MQTT. You register its node ID so the packets have an owner.
page.start.basics.node.title: Node
page.start.basics.node.body: A node is any other radio on the mesh. Nodes show up here once the gateway has forwarded a packet from them.
page.start.basics.reading.title: Reading
page.start.basics.reading.body: A reading is one measurement from a node, stored after the packet is decrypted.
page.start.mesh.title: Create your mesh
page.start.mesh.help: Copy the channel name and key from the Meshtastic app.
page.start.register.title: Register your gateway
page.start.register.help: The node ID is on the radio's screen or in the Meshtastic app, as hex (with or without !) or as a decimal number.
page.start.connect.title: Connect the gateway
page.start.connect.admin: Ask your Mesh Things administrator for the broker host, port, and gateway login.
page.start.connect.error: The broker details didn't load. Try again.
page.start.connect.uplink: In the Meshtastic app, enable MQTT and uplink on the {channel} channel, and leave encryption on. Leave the root topic at its default.
page.start.connect.waiting: Waiting for the gateway. This starts once the radio publishes.
page.start.connect.connected: Gateway connected. A packet has arrived.
page.start.connect.pollError: The last check didn't reach the server. We'll keep trying.
page.start.connect.check.network: The gateway has a network connection.
page.start.connect.check.channel: The channel name matches {channel}, including capitals.
page.start.connect.check.uplink: Uplink is on for that channel.
page.start.next.title: What you can do next
page.start.next.alarms: Alarms live under Alarms in the console. They email you when a reading leaves the range you set.
page.start.next.blueprints: Blueprints live under Blueprints. A blueprint derives a new channel from readings a device already sends.
page.start.next.toggleHelp: The email goes to this account after several missed intervals. One gap does not send it.
page.start.next.error: That setting didn't save. Check your connection and try again.
page.start.done.title: Your mesh is set up
page.start.meshMissing.title: That mesh was not found
page.start.meshMissing.body: It does not exist, or it belongs to another account. You can start a new mesh.
figure.check-email.title: Check the mailbox
figure.check-email.aria: Scrub the mailbox from the letter arriving to the lamp confirming the link
figure.check-email.svg: Kerbside mailbox with a red flag and a 60-second resend dial
figure.check-email.key.flag: Flag up: the message was sent
figure.check-email.key.lamp: Lamp on: the link was opened
figure.check-email.caption: A letter drops in and the flag rises. The dial runs the 60-second resend wait down to zero, then the door opens, the letter is taken and the lamp lights. This step checks every 5 seconds and continues on its own.
figure.basics.aria: Relay bench, from the radios to the database
figure.register.title: Read the node ID
figure.register.caption: Eight wheels set the hex node ID. The radio screen shows the short name (the last four digits) and the full ID, the same ID the Meshtastic app shows as hex or decimal.
figure.register.label: Meshtastic radio showing a node ID beside eight hex wheels
figure.connect.aria: Gateway toggles on the phone. Arrows pick a toggle, up and down or space flip it, home and end set them all.
figure.connect.title: Connect the gateway
figure.connect.key.packet: Packet to the broker once the gateway is seen
figure.connect.caption: The phone runs the Meshtastic app and links to the gateway node over Bluetooth LE. On the screen, top to bottom, the toggles are MQTT, uplink and encryption. Only when all three are on does the radio show Wi-Fi arcs and a packet travel over Wi-Fi to the MQTT broker, and the seen lamp on the broker lights. The page checks every 5 seconds.
figure.connect.label: Phone with MQTT, uplink and encryption toggles, linked by Bluetooth to the gateway node. The packet reaches the broker when all three are on.
figure.next-steps.title: Alarms and blueprints
figure.next-steps.caption: A sensor node with a BME280 sends the temperature over LoRa. The dial alarms when that reading leaves the range you set. The slide rule is a blueprint: it turns the same reading into a new channel, so {reading} °C is {derived} °F. Drag the dial or use the arrow keys. Up and down move the high set-point; Shift moves the low one.
figure.next-steps.label: Sensor node with a BME280 sending the temperature over the air to a panel thermometer with two set-point pointers, an alarm bell and an envelope chute, beside a slide rule. Drag to move the reading.
figure.next-steps.value: {reading} degrees, range {min} to {max}, {state}. Left and right move the reading. Up and down move the high set-point. Shift up and down moves the low set-point.
figure.done.title: Watchdog dial
figure.done.caption: Three nodes and the gateway share the bench. Packets hop over the air to the gateway, which sends them over Wi-Fi to Mesh Things. Each packet rewinds the dial. The email flag drops after the default of three missed half-hour intervals.
figure.done.stage: Three nodes, a gateway on a mast, and a watchdog dial. Hold to pause packets.
